Sales_Ana: Heads-up — Velaris (enterprise) plans a sustained integration test in eu-west1 tomorrow 08:30 UTC for ~4h. They expect ~80 r/s hitting text-generation (rw-serve-large), ~150 tokens per response. We need to avoid admission drops for their account (velaris-prod). Can we get a short-term quota exception or routing change? :pray:
EngInfra_Ravi: Thanks — can you confirm: region=eu-west1, model=rw-serve-large, sustained QPS=80, avg tokens=150, duration~4h, account=velaris-prod? Any wiggle room on start time?
Sales_Ana: Confirmed all of that. Start is firm at 08:30 UTC. No can do on shifting start. This is part of a paid proof-of-concept — sales will absorb overage.
EngSRE_Liam: Noted. Current admission-control metrics for eu-west1 look like this (pulled just now):
```
# metrics
admission_drops_total{region="eu-west1"} 1245
queue_depth{pool="shared-inference"} 42
tokens_in_flight{region="eu-west1"} 98000
```
If we accept 80 r/s * 150 tokens = 12k tokens/s sustained for Velaris, queueing will increase unless we shift capacity or loosen per-tenant caps.
EngInfra_Ravi: Two options: 1) temporary per-tenant rate cap bump for velaris-prod + soft-priority admission policy (lets Velaris preempt shared queueing up to a limit), or 2) reassign 2 GPUs from pre-reserved lower-priority pool into eu-west1 inference pool for the window. Option 1 is lower infra change surface but increases interference risk; option 2 increases infra cost but is safer for SLOs. Which does Sales prefer?
Finance_Eve: If we reassign GPUs or increase billing exposure we need sales sign-off for overage/costs. Sales_Ana, please confirm Velaris will accept billed overage and whether we invoice immediately or roll into contract.
Sales_Ana: Velaris confirms they accept billed overage and prefer invoice rolled into contract. Proceed with whatever minimizes risk to platform stability.
Support_Maya: I'll draft runbook for the operation and rollback window. Proposed runbook (short):
1) Create admission policy: allow velaris-prod up to 14k tokens/s with soft priority key velaris-prod-temp
2) Monitor admission_drops_total and queue_depth every 2m for 2h after start
3) If tail latency > 2x SLO for any other tenant, rollback immediately
4) Auto-revert policy at 12:45 UTC (15m after end window)
Command to apply (internal tool):
```
fleetctl policy apply --region eu-west1 --name velaris-temp --body '{"tenant":"velaris-prod","tokens_per_sec":14000,"priority":"soft"}'
```
Who will run step 1?
EngSRE_Liam: I can run step 1 at T-15 and monitor. I'll also add a temporary metric alert for per-tenant tail latency.
deploy-bot: policy-change: velaris-temp applied by EngSRE_Liam at 1801235700
EngSRE_Liam: Applied now. First 5m checks: queue_depth down from 42 -> 22, admission_drops_total rate falling. Initial latency for shared tenants stable. :thumbsup:
EngInfra_Ravi: Good. I'll standby to reassign GPUs if we see degradation. Keep me looped if the alert fires.
Finance_Eve: Noted billing preference; I'll update the sales order to include the overage.
CustomerSuccess_Joel: I'll coordinate with Velaris to confirm they actually ramp as planned and collect traces if they hit issues. Please send me the test run IDs or request ids so I can link telemetry.
EngSRE_Liam: Monitoring looks green at +30m. Marking the temporary policy as active and scheduled to auto-revert at 12:45 UTC. I'll post a short follow-up when it's reverted and then we can do a quick async postmortem if anything popped up.
Sales_Ana: Thanks team — Velaris appreciates the fast turnaround.
EngSRE_Liam: Revert executed at 1801237600. Metrics returned to baseline; no SLO breaches recorded. Will file postmortem with request/alert graphs.
Support_Maya: Added notes to the incident runbook and created a follow-up thread for the postmortem.
CustomerSuccess_Joel: I'll loop in Velaris and share the test report after we get the PM notes.
EngInfra_Ravi: Closing the action items on infra side. Will open a ticket to consider permanent capacity reservation options for Velaris if they plan repeated windows.
Sales_Ana: Great, thanks everyone :raised_hands:
